chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Comedy gags in the act: skis, window shades and the piano push
summary: He recites two-person question-and-answer gags, the piano-pushing bit later used on the Dean Martin show.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, you've described your act. I'd like to go a little bit further into your act because you talk about some gags you did. You did tell me the gag about the bear before. And it seems like gags were interdispersed throughout the act. What other kinds of gags were there?
It takes two people to do them, the other gags. Questions and answers. Such as, I say to my partner, he being short, I says and he had big shoes on,

so I says, "Are them skis you got on? Your feet sure is big. How do you get your pants off at night?" "I pull them off over my head," And I says, "Well you pull this off over your head," and I starts playing and he starts dancing.

First I say, "Get out of that hole." "I ain't in no hole." "You sure is a low man, you know." And I start playing for him to dance. He dances and then he comes back to the piano and plays for me to dance.

And I say, "I passed by your house last night. Yeah, I saw you kissing your wife. Now, why didn't you put your window shades down? How come? I saw you kissing your wife. Ha-ha-ha-ha." "What you laughing about, I wasn't even home last night." That's a scorcher, man, that's a scorcher gag. That gag kicks them around like a dog.
One of our gags -- we enter with a piano, you know, we come on, he pushes the piano and I'm at the front end of the piano,

"Push on it, push on it." He says, "I'm pushing on it." "No, you ain't, you're leaning on it." "Don't you be hollering at me." "They ain't nobody hollering at you, man. That mouth of yours will get the rest of your body in trouble," says I to him, see? He says to me, "I don't have to push on the piano, I can play the piano." Then he starts to play. Our gag is, push on your end, my end will follow and I'm in front. That's a big laugh they got on the Dean Martin show with that pulling gag. Push on your end, mine will follow.
Well, that was a gag we pulled and played piano selections and came into the dance. You got the whole act.
